title: Concrete Security Bound for LR6 Outer-Keyed Sponges
summary: Existing bounds requiring a uniformly sampled PKEM key do not directly apply to a derived key; obtain a concrete bound for the LR6-instantiated outer-keyed sponge.

formal_statement.body: For an outer-keyed sponge, the initial $b$-bit PKEM key $L$ is derived from $K$ by the key-derivation function rather than sampled uniformly, so existing bounds that require a uniformly selected $L$ cannot be directly applied. When the sponge permutation is instantiated by the six-round keyless Feistel construction $\mathrm{LR6}$, derive a concrete security bound for this setting, with the sponge rate $r$ and capacity $c$ as parameters.

scope.domain: Concrete security analysis of outer-keyed sponges instantiated with the six-round keyless Feistel construction LR6.
assumptions: The initial PKEM key L is derived from K by the key-derivation function rather than sampled uniformly.
parameters: b: bit length of the initial PKEM key L
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive a concrete security bound for the LR6-instantiated outer-keyed sponge with a derived PKEM key, using the sponge rate and capacity as parameters.

citations.label: Revisiting Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers for Shorter Keys and Multi-user Security

progress.summary: The source explains that existing bounds cannot be directly applied because the PKEM key is derived rather than uniformly chosen. It leaves a concrete bound open while identifying LR6 as a secure permutation instantiation.
citation_labels: Chun Guo et al., Revisiting Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers for Shorter Keys and Multi-user Security
